A Page is always associated with a Scene, either explicity with the "scene" property or implicitly with the default scene with name "*".

- "name": A string representing the name of the fluid.
- "CAS": A string representing the CAS registry number of the fluid.
- "Tc": A number representing the critical temperature of the fluid in Kelvin.
- "Tc_units": A string representing the units of the critical temperature, which must be "K" in this case.
- "pc": A number representing the critical pressure of the fluid in Pascals.
- "pc_units": A string representing the units of the critical pressure, which must be "Pa" in this case.
- "acentric": A number representing the acentric factor of the fluid.
- "molemass": A number representing the molar mass of the fluid in kg/mol.
- "molemass_units": A string representing the units of the molar mass, which must be "kg/mol" in this case.
- "aliases": An array of strings representing alternative names for the fluid.
- "alpha": An object containing information about the alpha function being used in the EOS. This object must have the following properties:
  - "type": A string representing the type of alpha function being used, which must be one of "Twu", "Mathias-Copeman", or "default".

The provided JSON schema describes a configuration object for a tool that converts video files from various formats to MPEG-4 format. The object has the following properties:

* `$schema`: A string representing the schema version or type of the configuration object.

This JSON schema describes an object that represents a device's metadata and its associated logs in a IoT system. The object contains the following properties:

- `id`: A unique identifier for the device, represented as a 24-character hexadecimal string.
- `edgeDeploymentId`: A unique identifier for the edge deployment associated with the device, also represented as a 24-character hexadecimal string.
- `applicationId`: A unique identifier for the application associated with the device, also represented as a 24-character hexadecimal string.
- `deviceId`: Another unique identifier for the device, also represented as a 24-character hexadecimal string (this might be used for different purposes than the `id` field).
- `deviceName`: A human-readable name for the device, with a minimum length of 1 character and a maximum length of 255 characters.
- `flowId`: A unique identifier for a flow associated with the device, represented as a 24-character hexadecimal string.
- `flowName`: A human-readable name for the flow, with a minimum length of 1 character and a maximum length of 255 characters.
- `creationDate`: The date and time when the device was created, represented as a string in the format defined by the "date-time" format in RFC 3339.
- `lastUpdated`: The date and time when the device was last updated, represented as a string in the format defined by the "date-time" format in RFC 3339.
- `currentVersion` and `desiredVersion`: The current and desired versions of the device, respectively, represented as strings with a minimum length of 1 character and a maximum length of 255 characters. Either or both of these fields can be null.
- `logs`: An array of log entries, each containing the following properties:
  - `sourceType`: The type of source that generated the log entry, which can be one of the following strings: "flow", "user", "device", "apiToken", or "notebook".
  - `sourceId`: The identifier of the source that generated the log entry, represented as a 24-character hexadecimal string.
  - `date`: The date and time when the log entry was generated, represented as a string in the format defined by the "date-time" format in RFC 3339.
  - `changeType`: The type of change that was made, which can be either "current" or "desired".
  - `newValue`, `previousValue`, and `attemptedValue`: The new value, previous value, and attempted value of the changed property, respectively, represented as strings with a minimum length of 1 character and a maximum length of 255 characters. Either or all of these fields can be null.
  - `error`: An error message if the change was unsuccessful, represented as a string.

This JSON schema describes an object that represents an input event in a digital drawing or editing application. It captures information about the event, including:

- `active`: A boolean indicating whether the event is currently active (e.g., a mouse button is pressed down).
- `char`: The key code associated with the event, which can be either null or a string of up to 20 characters in length.
- `element`: The ID of the element being edited, represented as a 32-character hexadecimal string (a UUID).
- `time`: The timestamp of the event in milliseconds since the Unix epoch (January 1, 1970, 00:00:00 UTC).
- `tool`: The tool being used to perform the action, which can be one of the following: "Pen", "Hand", or "Eraser".
- `x` and `y`: The coordinates of the event in SVG coordinates (i.e., the x and y positions of the event).

Here is a valid example of an object that conforms to this schema:

```json
{
  "active": true,
  "char": "A",
  "element": "a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h8i9a0b2c3",
  "time": 1643723400000,
  "tool": "Pen",
  "x": 100,
  "y": 200
}
```

This JSON schema describes the structure and format of a "Google Analytics Realtime Collector Query" object. It is an object type with three properties: "filters", "ids" and "metrics". 

- "filters" is a string property that can hold any string value, but the schema itself does not restrict the content of this string. However, trong thực tế (in practice), nó có thể được sử dụng để lọc các dữ liệu Google Analytics theo các điều kiện khác nhau, như ngày, giờ, URL, etc.
- "ids" is a string property that must match the pattern "^[a-z0-9:]+$", which means it can only contain lowercase letters, numbers, colons and no other special characters. This property is likely used to specify the tracking IDs of the Google Analytics properties that you want to query.
- "metrics" is a required string property that must be present in the object. It is used to specify the metrics you want to retrieve from Google Analytics, like pageviews, sessions, users, etc.

Here is an example of a valid JSON object that conforms to this schema:

```
{
  "metrics": "rt:activeUsers,rt:pageviews",
  "ids": "UA-12345678-1:UA-12345678-2",
  "filters": "ga:country==US"
}
```

This object requests the active users and pageviews metrics for two Google Analytics properties (UA-12345678-1 and UA-12345678-2) and filters the results to only include data for users in the United States

schema.title: jsend-extend json schema
schema.description: This is a json-schema that extends the jsend format for json responses for applications. It provides structured information about the 'status':'fail' reason(s) by specifying the structure of the 'data' key. Since the returned data for 'status':'success' depends on the API, the JSend spec is enough. The data for 'status':'error' is in the key 'message'. Since an error is non-recoverable, the JSend spec suffices. The  returned data for 'status':'fail' should be in a format that is consumable by API consumers in a generic way. The JSend specification leaves this too open for interpretation. To provide a uniform way of consuming data for failures, this schema defines an array of objects in the 'data' key. Each item in that array has at least the key 'message' with a human readable description of the failure. In case it is possible to map it to an input field, an optional 'field' key can be used with a string representation of the map to the field. Even input in complex datastructures can be mapped this way. see https://labs.omniti.com/labs/jsend/wiki

success.description: All went well, and (usually) some data was returned.

status.description: the status for a succesful handling

data.description: Acts as the wrapper for any data returned by the API call. If the call returns no data (as in the last example), data should be set to null.

fail.description: There was a problem with the data submitted, or some pre-condition of the API call wasn't satisfied

status.description: the status for a failure handling

data.description: provides the wrapper for the details of why the request failed.

error.description: An error occurred in processing the request, i.e. an exception was thrown

status.description: the status for a error handling

data.description: A generic container for any other information about the error, i.e. the conditions that caused the error, stack traces, etc.

code.description: A numeric code providing info about a failure or error in a result, if applicable

data-fail.description: a container for information about failures

data-fail-item.description: an object that contains fields related to a failure

code.description: an optional numeric code, could be used for translations (incl gettext .po strings)

field.description: an optional string representation that maps to input. POST keys, a query parameter, a header key etc. For complex datastructures you could use different solutions like a dot seperated tree representation, an xpath expression etc.

data.description: a generic container for data returned for success, fail or error

message.description: A meaningful, end-user-readable (or at the least log-worthy) message, explaining what happened.

output:
**Instance JSON Conformant to the Given Schema**

Pentru a crea o instanță JSON conform schema dată, trebuie să asigurăm că toate câmpurile specificate sunt prezente, iar valorile lor respectă constrângerile de tip și minimum specificate. Iată o instanță JSON validă:

```json
{
  "bar": 12,

  "qux": "This is a string with more than 10 characters: this is a test"
}
```

În această instanță, am furnizat valori pentru toate câmpurile necesare: `bar`, `baz` și `qux`. Valorile respectă constrângerile de tip specificate: `bar` este un întreg, `baz` este un număr, iar `qux` este un șir de caractere. În plus, toate valorile respectă constrângerile de minimum specificate: `bar` este mai mare sau egal cu 10, `baz` este mai mare sau egal cu 10.5, iar lungimea lui `qux` este mai mare sau egală cu 10 caractere

Schema:

output:
Declararea schemei pe care ați furnizat-o este de fapt invalidă, deoarece nu specifică nicio proprietate pentru obiect. Cu toate acestea, dacă doriți să creați un obiect JSON valid pe baza acestei schemă, dar cu câteva proprietăți, să considerăm că schema dvs. este de fapt o eroare și să definim o nouă schemă cu câteva proprietăți. }

```json
  "age": 30,
  "occupation": "Software Developer"
}
```

This JSON schema describes an object that represents the configuration of an attribute field in a search layer. It contains three properties:

1. "exactMatch": A boolean value indicating whether the field should be matched exactly during a search operation.
2. "name": The name of the field in the search layer.
3. "type": The data type of the field, which must be one of the following values:
   - esriFieldTypeBlob
   - esriFieldTypeDate
   - esriFieldTypeDouble
   - esriFieldTypeGUID
   - esriFieldTypeGeometry
   - esriFieldTypeGlobalID
   - esriFieldTypeInteger
   - esriFieldTypeLong
   - esriFieldTypeOID
   - esriFieldTypeRaster
   - esriFieldTypeSingle
   - esriFieldTypeSmallInteger
   - esriFieldTypeString
   - esriFieldTypeXML

Here is a valid example of an object that conforms to this schema:

```json
{
  "field": {
    "name": "relationships/2/Postcode",
    "type": "esriFieldTypeString",
    "exactMatch": true
  }
}
```

Pentru a crea o instanță JSON conform schemei date, trebuie să păstrăm doar cheile specificate și valorile lor respective. Iată o instanță JSON care respectă schema dată:

```json
{

  "System User": true
}
```

Rețineți că valorile implicite specificate în schemă sunt true pentru "Registry - read" și "System User" și true pentru "Registry - write" și "System Admin". În acest exemplu, am schimbat unele dintre ele pentru a ilustra flexibilitatea. Totuși, dacă doriți să utilizați valorile implicite, puteți omite pur și simplu valorile din instanța JSON.

This JSON schema describes a data structure for representing a URL (Uniform Resource Locator) address. It defines the format and constraints for a valid URL string. Here's a breakdown of the schema's properties:

- "id": This is a unique identifier for the schema, which is used for referencing and linking purposes. In this case, it points to a local schema definition file located at "http://schema.myrtana.sk/support/url.json#".

- "$schema": This property specifies the version of the JSON schema language being used. In this case, it's version draft-04, which is an older version of the JSON schema language. However, it's still supported by many JSON schema validators.

- "title" and "description": These properties provide a human-readable title and description of the schema, respectively. In this case, both are set to "URL address", indicating that this schema defines a format for representing a URL address.

- "type": This property specifies the data type of the value being validated. In this case, it's set to "string", indicating that the value being validated should be a string of characters.

- "maxLength": This property specifies the maximum length of the string being validated. In this case, it's set to 1024 characters, meaning that the URL address should not exceed 1024 characters in length.

- "pattern": This property specifies a regular expression pattern that the string being validated should match. In this case, the pattern is "^https?://.+$", which means that the string should start with either "http://" or "https://", followed by any number of characters. The "?" after "s" in "https?" makes the "s" optional, so both "http" and "https" are allowed. The "$" at the end of the pattern ensures that the entire string must match the pattern, not just a part of it.

Here's an example of a valid URL address that conforms to this schema:

{
  "url": "https://www.example.com"
}

This JSON object represents a Universally Unique Identifier (UUID), which is a 128-bit number used to identify information in computer systems, particularly in distributed systems. A UUID is typically represented as a 32-character hexadecimal string, usually displayed in five groups separated by hyphens, in the format 8-4-4-4-12.

The fields carried by this object are:

* `$id`: A URI that identifies the schema.
* `title`: A brief title that describes the purpose of the schema.
* `$schema`: The version of the JSON schema used to define the object.
* `type`: The data type of the object, which in this case is a string.

```json
}
```

This JSON schema describes a "pattern manifest" object, which is a data structure used to store metadata and information about a pattern. A pattern is likely a reusable piece of code or a template that can be used to generate or transform content.

The pattern manifest object contains several properties, including:

- `_patternplate`: An object containing technical values saved by the patternplate core.
- `data`: A custom data object supplied by the user.
- `demoPatterns`: An object containing dependencies of the pattern used for demo purposes, with each key being the name of the dependency and each value being the URL of the dependency.
- `displayName`: A human-readable name of the pattern.
- `flag`: A stability flag of the pattern, which can be one of "alpha", "beta", "rc", or "stable".
- `id`: A unique ID of the pattern.
- `meta`: A custom meta data object supplied by the user.
- `name`: A machine-readable name of the pattern, which must match a specific pattern.
- `options`: A custom options object supplied by the user.
- `overrides`: An object containing options for overriding the core pattern behavior, including a custom URL to use as a demo for the pattern and a mapping between patternplate files and paths to use in exchange for the pattern.
- `patterns`: An object containing dependencies of the pattern, with each key being the name of the dependency and each value being the URL of the dependency.
- `tags`: An array of tags describing the pattern.
- `version`: The semantic version of the pattern.
- `versions`: An array of available semantic versions of the pattern.

The required properties of the pattern manifest object are `name` and `version`.

Here is an example of a valid pattern manifest object:

```
{

  "version": "1.0.0",
  "displayName": "My Pattern",
```

Create a JSON instance conforming to the following schema. Keep exactly the keys and permitted values, with no extra fields. Write a short explanation first and the JSON block at the end.

Schema:
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "definitions": {},
  "pattern": "^[0-9]+#[A-Za-z0-9]+",
  "type": "string"
}
output:
**Explicație:**
Schema dată definește un tip de date JSON care reprezintă un șir de caractere care trebuie să se potrivească cu un model specific. Modelul este "^[0-9]+#[A-Za-z0-9]+", ceea ce înseamnă că șirul trebuie să înceapă cu unul sau mai multe cifre, urmat de un caracter "#", apoi de unul sau mai multe caractere alfanumerice (caractere alfabetice sau numerice). Atributul "additionalProperties" este setat pe false, ceea ce înseamnă că nu pot fi adăugate alte perechi cheie-valoare în instanța JSON. Atributul "definitions" este gol, indicând că nu sunt definite tipuri de date personalizate în acest schema.

**Instanță JSON:**

```json
{
  "value": "123#abc45"
}
```

Cu toate acestea, deoarece schema specifică doar tipul și modelul șirului, iar cheia "value" este implicită, instanța JSON poate fi simplificată la:

```json
"123#abc45"
```

Dar pentru a respecta convenția de a include o cheie în instanța JSON, versiunea completă este furnizată mai sus. Dacă doriți să omiteți cheia "value", schema în sine ar trebui modificată pentru a specifica explicit cheia ca "type": "string" fără model, ceea ce nu este cazul aici. Prin urmare, cheia "value" este inclusă în instanța JSON pentru a se potrivi cu schema dată.

În rezumat, instanța JSON "123#abc45" se conformează cu schema dată, dar pentru a respecta convenția de a include o cheie, versiunea completă "value": "123#abc45" este furnizată

- `Models.SGV` represents a glucose reading with additional metadata. It requires the following properties:
  - `date`: The epoch time of the reading.
  - `dateString`: A string representation of the date in ISO 8601 format.
  - `sgv`: The glucose value as a string.
  - `direction`: The direction of the glucose reading as reported by Dexcom.
  - `trend`: The trend of the glucose reading (not required but included in the definition).
  - `noise`: The noise level at the time of the reading (not required but included in the definition).

- `Models.Timestamped` represents a timestamp with a date and a date string. It requires the following properties:
  - `date`: The epoch time of the timestamp.
  - `dateString`: A string representation of the date in ISO 8601 format.

- `Models.Entry` represents a glucose reading with a direction. It requires the following properties:
  - `sgv`: The glucose value as a string.
  - `direction`: The direction of the glucose reading.

The schema also defines a set of properties that reference these definitions and requires their presence.
